title: How to Create More Buy-In
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that a leader's real power comes from buy-in rather than formal authority, and it lays out both the well-known and lesser-known practices behind earning it. Familiar tactics include seeking input early, cultivating champions, and clearly articulating milestones and benefits. Less obvious, the piece says, is the behind-the-scenes work: leaders who gain genuine buy-in demonstrate their own conviction first, work resistance through many individual conversations, and resist the urge to simply hand people decisions. Instead, they invite collaboration and let the team help build the path forward, which is what ultimately produces lasting commitment.
points: Buy-in, not authority, is what actually drives team execution and effort.
Common buy-in tactics include early input, identifying champions, and clear milestones.
The best leaders demonstrate their own conviction before asking others to commit.
Great leaders avoid simply handing out decisions and instead ask people what they want to do together.
Buy-in starts with collaboration and builds momentum through ongoing dialogue.
quotes: The true source of power for a leader is not authority but buy-in.
How to create more buy-in is the master skill of great leadership.
Without buy-in, even a great decision or strategy is abandoned by the team and only realizes a small part of its full potential.
They are quick to demonstrate their own buy-in before asking others to do so, often going to great lengths to showcase their conviction in group settings.
People get on board slow-moving trains where leaders ask them to collaborate to build a railroad.
They don’t sell or direct. They involve and collaborate. And buy-in is the result.
